XXXIII ACMM MEMBER-MACT, BENGALURU. PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant, calling in question the judgment and award dated 10.10.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.3902/2016, on the file of the VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) for seeking enhancement of the compensation.

Brief facts:
2. On 27.01.2016 at about 1.30 p.m., the claimant was walking on extreme left side of Nagarabhavi Ring Road, near Vokkaligara Sangha College, rider of Suzuki Access Scooter bearing registration No.KA-02-HZ-9269, came with high speed in rash and negligent manner from Kottigepalya towards Papareddipalya and dashed against him, as a result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3.
Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part,
and awarded a compensation of Rs.3,12,500/-, along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent No.1 - insurance company, liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.1 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.

5. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
 Pain and Suffering : Rs. 50,000/-

Medical Expenses : Rs. 1,20,000/-
 Nourishing Food : Rs. 15,000/-
 Loss of Earnings During Treatment : Rs. 92,500/-
 period  Future medical expenses : Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of Amenities : Rs. 10,000/-
 TOTAL : Rs. 3,12,500/-
6.

As per the Wound Certificate at Exhibit-P7, Discharge Summary and Exhibit-P8, coupled with the evidence of PW-2, Doctor and the documentary evidence, it is proved that the claimant had suffered fracture of left limb, fracture of distal radius left and abrasion of left knee.
The aforesaid injuries are grievous in nature.
The compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal under each head viz., pain and sufferings, loss of amenities, future medical expenses are on lesser side.

Hence, the appellant- claimant is awarded an additional global compensation of Rs.70,000/- along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of total compensation within Eight Weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.

7. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 10.10.2017, passed in M.V.C.No.3902/2016, on the file of the VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, is modified to the aforesaid extent.
iii. The appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional global compensation of Rs.70,000/- along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

iv. Respondent No.1 - insurance company shall Sri Kempanna vs Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178510895/
3  pay the compensation to the  appellant/claimant.
